topic: Central Limit Theorem: The Magic of the Bell Curve
target_audience: University students taking introductory statistics or data science

sections.title: The Mystery of Predictable Chaos
lecture_lines: Welcome to the world of unpredictable and chaotic data.
Imagine a forest filled with giant, oddly weighted squirrels.
Individual weights are messy, following no specific pattern.
animations: Create a scatter of 15 squirrel icons with varying sizes (1kg to 20kg) spread across the screen in #FFFFFF.
Transition the squirrels into a flat histogram on a horizontal axis, showing no clear pattern or normality.
Highlight a single squirrel icon in #FFFF00 and place a large '?' above it to emphasize unpredictability.

sections.title: Prerequisite Kit: Populations and Samples
lecture_lines: Let's define our population: a bag of diverse marbles.
A sample is just a small scoop from that bag.
The sample mean represents the average of that scoop.
animations: Display a large 'Population' container (#FFFFFF) filled with 100 varied data points.
Use a green circle (#00FF00) to select a small 'Sample' of 5 points from the container.
Move the selected points to a side area and display a calculated 'Sample Mean' value next to them.

sections.title: The Experiment: Gathering the Averages
lecture_lines: We repeatedly take random samples of thirty squirrels each.
Instead of plotting individuals, we calculate each group's average.
These averages are recorded on a new distribution graph.
Watch as each new average falls into its slot.
A familiar shape slowly begins to emerge from chaos.
animations: Show a faded, messy population distribution in the top half of the screen.
Animate a sampling box (#00FF00) repeatedly grabbing groups of 30 points from the population.
For each sample, drop a small dot onto a new horizontal axis at the bottom.
Show the dots stacking up into bars as more samples are taken (up to 1000 samples).
Highlight the emerging shape of the stack with a faint outline to show progress.

sections.title: The Grand Reveal: The Bell Curve Emerges
lecture_lines: The Central Limit Theorem reveals a hidden mathematical law.
As sample size grows, the distribution shape transforms.
Uniform or skewed data eventually yields a bell curve.
This normal distribution is symmetrical and highly predictable.
Large samples always find order within the original mess.
animations: Start with a skewed population distribution and a wide sampling distribution histogram.
Animate a slider for 'n' (sample size) increasing from 2 up to 30.
As 'n' increases, visually contract the sampling distribution bars toward the center.
Fade in a smooth Cyan (#00FFFF) Bell Curve that perfectly overlays the final histogram.
Flash the Bell Curve in #FFFFFF to signify the 'Grand Reveal' of the CLT.

sections.title: The Mathematical Pillars
lecture_lines: The mean of averages equals the original population mean.
Larger samples create a much narrower and taller curve.
This increased precision reduces our overall margin of error.
Typically, a sample size of thirty is the magic number.
Mathematics provides certainty even when starting with chaos.
animations: Position the Bell Curve centrally with its peak aligned to a vertical line labeled mu (#FFD700).
Display the Standard Error formula: sigma / sqrt(n) in the upper right corner (#FFFFFF).
Animate the 'n' in the denominator growing, causing the Bell Curve to become narrower and taller.
Display the text 'Magic Number: n >= 30' in #00FF00 at the bottom.
Highlight the property that the center of the sampling distribution is exactly the population mean.

sections.title: Why It Matters: The Statistician's Superpower
lecture_lines: This theorem is a superpower for predicting population behavior.
Factories use it to guarantee product quality and safety.
We find order in complexity through the bell curve.
animations: Display a factory setting with a conveyor belt of battery icons.
Draw a Bell Curve over a small sample of tested batteries to represent the whole batch.
Show the final conclusion text 'Predicting the Unknown' in #FFFFFF as the scene fades out.
